1: ## 1. Render hygiene micro-fixes (foundation, ~1 PR)
2: 
3: - [ ] 1.1 Wrap `LocationContext.Provider` value in `useMemo` in `src/context/LocationContext.jsx` (around line 182), with deps including only the underlying state values
4: - [ ] 1.2 Identify and list the ~20 pure utility functions currently inside `Calendar.jsx` (lines ~1127–1370) that close over no component state or props
5: - [ ] 1.3 Create `src/utils/calendarEventUtils.js` and move those pure utilities to module scope; update `Calendar.jsx` imports

8: - [ ] 1.6 Add a frontend test asserting `LocationContext` consumers do not re-render solely from provider re-creation
9: - [ ] 1.7 Add a frontend test asserting `MonthView` skips its render path when its inputs are referentially stable

13: ## 2. queryClient conventions and key factory
14: 
15: - [ ] 2.1 Document query-key conventions in a comment block in `src/config/queryClient.js` (resource-name first, scope discriminators after)
16: - [ ] 2.2 Create `src/queries/keys.js` exporting a minimal key factory (`keys.events.list({ view, ... })`, `keys.events.detail(eventId)`, `keys.reservations.list({ ... })`)
17: - [ ] 2.3 Update the existing RQ consumers (`useCategoriesQuery.js`, `useLocationsQuery.js`, `EventSearch.jsx`) to use the factory where applicable; do not break their current behavior
18: 
19: ## 3. MyReservations → React Query
20: 
21: - [ ] 3.1 Inventory every fetch + useEffect + useState + dispatchRefresh site in `MyReservations.jsx`
22: - [ ] 3.2 Replace each read with `useQuery` using factory-derived query keys
23: - [ ] 3.3 Replace each write (cancel, restore, edit, draft save/submit, etc.) with `useMutation` including `onMutate` (optimistic), `onError` (rollback), `onSuccess`/`onSettled` (invalidate)
24: - [ ] 3.4 During migration, dual-publish: RQ mutations also call `dispatchRefresh` so non-migrated views still see updates
25: - [ ] 3.5 Add or update tests covering: cache hit on remount, optimistic update visible immediately, rollback on simulated error, invalidation on success
26: - [ ] 3.6 Browser-verify Edit / Delete / Restore / Resubmit flows end-to-end
27: - [ ] 3.7 Provide ready-to-use commit message

29: ## 4. ReservationRequests (Approval Queue) → React Query
30: 
31: - [ ] 4.1 Inventory every fetch + useEffect + useState + dispatchRefresh site in `ReservationRequests.jsx`
32: - [ ] 4.2 Replace reads with `useQuery` (counts query and list query each get their own key)
33: - [ ] 4.3 Replace approve / reject / restore / delete / publish-edit / reject-edit mutations with `useMutation` (optimistic + rollback + invalidate)
34: - [ ] 4.4 Verify cross-tab counter consistency (approving a pending event decrements the pending counter optimistically and increments the published counter)
35: - [ ] 4.5 Add or update tests for the new query/mutation patterns; cover the 409 conflict path's rollback
36: - [ ] 4.6 Browser-verify Approval Queue end-to-end (approve, reject, restore, delete, edit-request)
37: - [ ] 4.7 Provide ready-to-use commit message

39: ## 5. Backend hot-path fixes inside `routes/eventsList.js`

41: - [ ] 5.1 Create `backend/routes/eventsList.js` with an `express.Router()` (or factory) export
42: - [ ] 5.2 Move the handlers for `POST /api/events/load`, `GET /api/events/list`, and `GET /api/events/list/counts` from `api-server.js` into `routes/eventsList.js`; mount under `/api/events` from `api-server.js`
43: - [ ] 5.3 Run targeted backend tests for these endpoints; assert behavior is unchanged from the move alone
44: - [ ] 5.4 Replace the per-calendar Graph fetch loop in `POST /api/events/load` with `Promise.allSettled(...)`; preserve per-calendar try/catch semantics by treating rejected calendars as zero-event with structured warning log
45: - [ ] 5.5 Add a backend test that mocks one of three calendars to fail and asserts the request returns 200 with events from the surviving two
46: - [ ] 5.6 Gate `enrichSeriesMastersWithOverrides(...)` on `mastersFound > 0` in both `POST /api/events/load` and `GET /api/events/list`; preserve the cold-Cosmos retry path for the masters-present case
47: - [ ] 5.7 Add a backend test asserting enrichment is not invoked when the events query returned zero series masters
48: - [ ] 5.8 Add a Mongo projection to `GET /api/events/list` that excludes `graphData` from each returned document
49: - [ ] 5.9 Add a backend test asserting list response items contain no `graphData` field
50: - [ ] 5.10 Move the JS `Array.prototype.sort` for the list endpoint into the Mongo query (sort by `calendarData.startDateTime`)
51: - [ ] 5.11 Create the compound index `(status: 1, calendarData.startDateTime: 1)` on `templeEvents__Events` via an idempotent `createIndex` call (check the query-shape audit at extraction time to confirm whether `calendarOwner` should prefix the index)

53: - [ ] 5.13 Provide ready-to-use commit message

55: ## 6. OCC restoration on `audit-update`
56: 
57: - [ ] 6.1 Replace the bare `updateOne` in `POST /api/events/:eventId/audit-update` (`api-server.js:8195`, or its new home in `routes/events.js`) with `conditionalUpdate(...)` (or `findOneAndUpdate` with `_version` precondition)
58: - [ ] 6.2 Accept `expectedVersion` in the request body; treat `null`/missing as "skip version check" (backward compat)
59: - [ ] 6.3 Return the post-update document via `findOneAndUpdate({ returnDocument: 'after' })`; remove the redundant trailing `findOne` (`api-server.js:8270–8272`)
60: - [ ] 6.4 Add a backend test asserting concurrent `audit-update` calls produce the standard 409 `VERSION_CONFLICT` payload with field-level diff snapshot
61: - [ ] 6.5 Add a backend test asserting an omitted `expectedVersion` skips the version check (legacy-caller behavior preserved)
62: - [ ] 6.6 Provide ready-to-use commit message

80: ## 9. SSE → React Query bridge
81: 
82: - [ ] 9.1 In `src/hooks/useServerEvents.js`, translate `event-changed` SSE messages into `queryClient.invalidateQueries(...)` calls keyed by the broadcast's view/resource
83: - [ ] 9.2 When the SSE payload includes the full updated event document, additionally call `queryClient.setQueryData(['events', 'detail', eventId], updatedDoc)` and patch the matching entry inside the relevant `['events', 'list', ...]` cache
84: - [ ] 9.3 On `serverStartId` change, call `queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['events'] })` and `queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['reservations'] })`
85: - [ ] 9.4 Keep the legacy `dispatchRefresh` calls firing during the migration window (back-compat for non-migrated subscribers)
86: - [ ] 9.5 Add tests covering: invalidate on `event-changed`, `setQueryData` on full-payload broadcasts, restart-id-driven cross-cutting invalidation
